findings.title: Inner door 80 × 200 cm behind the blast door — optional, not a requirement
findings.detail: The safe-room doorway is drawn with two leaves: the steel blast door (opens outwards) and an ordinary inner door 80 × 200 cm that opens into the room. Status: the inner door is NOT required by the regulations. The Civil Defence regulations require one gas-tight blast door opening outwards (regs. 202(a), 204(a)) and do not mention a second, ordinary door for the safe room of a dwelling; they expressly allow "a regular door, opening inwards, for everyday use" in addition to the blast door only for protected spaces in health institutions (reg. 287(b)), and a second blast door only in place of the window, with approval (reg. 204(b2)). For a home it is an optional comfort feature that Home Front Command guidance is reported to permit (press report; not verified on the Home Front Command site) — ask the architect to confirm that the plan approved by the Home Front Command shows it. Conditions: the blast door, its frame and its seal stay untouched and are never removed; the inner door opens into the room and must not stop the blast door closing; keep its 80 cm arc inside the room free of furniture.

findings.title: Permit: Window — Bedroom 1 / outside: moved 60 cm
findings.detail: This changes an exterior wall opening, i.e. the outside of the building and its façade, so it is not an "internal change" (שינוי פנימי): under §145(a)(2) of the Planning and Building Law it has to be in the building permit — ask the architect to put it into the permit application, or to file an amendment if the permit was already issued, before it is built. Only swapping a window for one of the same size in the same place is exempt (exempt-works regulations, reg. 20(a)). The architect must also re-check the room's daylight, the lintel and the thermal calculation.
findings.reference: חוק התכנון והבניה, התשכ"ה-1965 — Planning and Building Law 1965 — §145(a)(2); Exempt-works regulations 2014, reg. 20(a) (like-for-like replacement). The procedure the local planning committee uses (amended permit / change during construction) and its spatial guidelines were not verified

findings.title: Inner door 80 × 200 cm behind the blast door — optional, not a requirement
findings.detail: The safe-room doorway is drawn with two leaves: the steel blast door (opens outwards) and an ordinary inner door 80 × 200 cm that opens into the room. Status: the inner door is NOT required by the regulations. The Civil Defence regulations require one gas-tight blast door opening outwards (regs. 202(a), 204(a)) and do not mention a second, ordinary door for the safe room of a dwelling; they expressly allow "a regular door, opening inwards, for everyday use" in addition to the blast door only for protected spaces in health institutions (reg. 287(b)), and a second blast door only in place of the window, with approval (reg. 204(b2)). For a home it is an optional comfort feature that Home Front Command guidance is reported to permit (press report; not verified on the Home Front Command site) — ask the architect to confirm that the plan approved by the Home Front Command shows it. Conditions: the blast door, its frame and its seal stay untouched and are never removed; the inner door opens into the room and must not stop the blast door closing; keep its 80 cm arc inside the room free of furniture.

findings.title: Inner door 80 × 200 cm behind the blast door — optional, not a requirement
findings.detail: The safe-room doorway is drawn with two leaves: the steel blast door (opens outwards) and an ordinary inner door 80 × 200 cm that opens into the room. Status: the inner door is NOT required by the regulations. The Civil Defence regulations require one gas-tight blast door opening outwards (regs. 202(a), 204(a)) and do not mention a second, ordinary door for the safe room of a dwelling; they expressly allow "a regular door, opening inwards, for everyday use" in addition to the blast door only for protected spaces in health institutions (reg. 287(b)), and a second blast door only in place of the window, with approval (reg. 204(b2)). For a home it is an optional comfort feature that Home Front Command guidance is reported to permit (press report; not verified on the Home Front Command site) — ask the architect to confirm that the plan approved by the Home Front Command shows it. Conditions: the blast door, its frame and its seal stay untouched and are never removed; the inner door opens into the room and must not stop the blast door closing; keep its 80 cm arc inside the room free of furniture.
